0|872fec16d9a0ed3b75b8893aa217e49cca575ee5|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"[PATCH] mm: init_mm without ptlock
First step in pushing down the page_table_lock.  init_mm.page_table_lock has
been used throughout the architectures (usually for ioremap): not to serialize
kernel address space allocation (that's usually vmlist_lock)
pud_alloc
Reverse that: don't lock or unlock init_mm.page_table_lock in any of the
architectures; instead rely on pud_alloc
and drop it when allocating a new one
column2: to check lest a racing task already

column1: did.  Similarly no page_table_lock in vmalloc's map_vm_area.
Some temporary ugliness in __pud_alloc and __pmd_alloc: since they also handle
user mms
column2: which are converted only by a later patch
column3: for now they have to lock

column1: differently according to whether or not it's init_mm.
If sources get muddled
column2: there's a danger that an arch source taking

column1: init_mm.page_table_lock will be mixed with common source also taking it (or
neither take it).  So break the rules and make another change
break the build for such a mismatch: remove the redundant mm arg from
pte_alloc_kernel (ppc64 scrapped its distinct ioremap_mm in 2.6.13).
Exceptions: arm26 used pte_alloc_kernel on user mm
used pte_alloc_map on init_mm
column2: now pte_alloc_kernel; parisc had bad args to

column1: pmd_alloc and pte_alloc_kernel in unused USE_HPPA_IOREMAP code; ppc64
map_io_page forgot to unlock on failure; ppc mmu_mapin_ram and ppc64 im_free
took page_table_lock for no good reason.
